summary: Hanimaadhoo International Airport (HAQ) is the main gateway to the northern Maldives, located on Hanimaadhoo Island in Haa Dhaalu Atoll. Originally a domestic airfield, it was upgraded to international status to reduce travel time to the remote northern atolls, which were previously only accessible via lengthy seaplane or domestic flights from Malé. The airport sits near the equator and serves as a vital hub for both tourism and local transport in this geographically isolated region.
faqs:
Q: How far is Hanimaadhoo Airport from Malé?
A: It is approximately 290 km north of Malé, with a typical flight time of around 50 minutes.

Q: Does the airport handle international flights?
A: Yes, it operates as an international airport with customs and immigration facilities, primarily serving routes from India and other South Asian destinations.

Q: Are there direct flights from Hanimaadhoo to Malé?
A: Yes, several Maldivian airlines operate regular scheduled flights between Hanimaadhoo and Velana International Airport in Malé.

Q: Can I reach resort islands from Hanimaadhoo Airport?
A: Yes, many resorts in the northern atolls arrange seaplane or speedboat transfers from this airport, which is closer than Malé for northern destinations.
transport_tips: Taxis and shared minivans are available on Hanimaadhoo Island to reach guesthouses and the harbor, though the island is small enough to walk or cycle. Speedboat transfers to nearby islands can be arranged in advance through resorts or local operators. Given the remote location, booking return transport well ahead of time is advisable, especially during off-peak periods when flight schedules may be limited.
local_tip: Pack a light jacket even on tropical trips—domestic turboprop flights can be quite cool due to strong air conditioning, and the open-air waiting areas at smaller atoll airports can be breezier than expected.
